title: Nubank's First Office: A Rented House on Rua Califórnia
conflicts: Launch: first card transactions 1 April 2014 (Sequoia podcast, Wikipedia) vs opening for business in September 2014 (TechCrunch 2014 and 2015, Época 2017); the story gives both as first transactions and public launch. How much the rule brought the launch forward: four months (Vélez, podcast) vs three months (Vélez, Stanford); story gives only the April 2014 deadline. Seed: April-May 2013 (Vélez) or May 2013 (Stanford) vs $2 million in July 2013 (TechCrunch EC-1); story says 2013, no amount. Bank-account wait five months (podcast) vs six (Época); story says months. Outcome numbers: Vélez's 2023 recollection of 5,000-10,000 sign-ups a day after a review does not square with TechCrunch's contemporary count of 200,000+ applications in eight months (100,000 waiting); the story uses TechCrunch's June 2015 figure only.
notes: The Sequoia Crucible Moments transcript is produced by Nubank's lead investor; claims from it are attributed to the speakers and the pivotal ones cross-checked with TechCrunch, Época Negócios and Stanford GSB. Wikipedia not cited. Xenophon's self-knowledge passage was my first choice but is already used in another edition, so Aristotle on deliberation (stance affirms) was used instead.
